cells.tense: Clear sight is arriving now and it has not yet cut into anything.
cells.act: follow the thought past where it is comfortable
cells.ask: Take one story this room tells about itself and follow it past the part you enjoy — down to what it cost and who goes unmentioned. Ten more minutes once it stops being comfortable, then leave it.
cells.core:
A new clarity is arriving and it hasn't cut into anything yet — just the plain ability to see what's here before anything specific gets made of it. You can read a tradition as a living thing and keep the seams showing while you do. Where something came from, what it carried, what it paid to carry: it's all in the same look.

Into the pattern, then, until you meet the edge of it. Take one of the stories this room tells about itself and follow it past the section you enjoy — back to where it came from, the debt, the part nobody sits next to. Ten more minutes once it stops being comfortable, then leave it. Depth is what happens when the pattern keeps going after you've recognized it. Nothing stale survives that. What's left is worth carrying, and it still carries.

cells.verb: seeing first, before there is anything to see

cells.tense: The next room will be braced against before you have arrived in it.
cells.act: carry what the spark became to its full size
cells.ask: Finish something you understand about a custom here — state it in full where it can finish, or set it down whole somewhere it will be found. Carry it to the end you saw.
cells.core:
In rooms where meaning is inherited, the shape of what's coming gets read early — what the holiday will mean, how the argument goes, what the word is going to do before anyone says it. So you come in before the room does, braced. After a while it's hard to stand anywhere you've been before, because the fresh edge is gone from it. What's on the far side is shining plainly because it is — nobody needs to be told.

What you understand about a custom here — a holiday, the way this group talks — likely stands finished already. Bring it out at its full size. State it in full where it can finish, or set it down whole where it will be found. It doesn't have to be neat. It just has to stop being carried. The next fresh thing gets to arrive with its own face.

cells.tense: You left off stepping into rooms and the leaving-off is what holds now.
cells.ask: Give a custom or saying you already use in some form a lasting shape this week — put it where it will be found again, or teach it once to somebody. Set it standing.
cells.core:
Seeing first stopped landing where meaning is shared. The older ways in this room read as the room's rather than yours, and you watch them from outside instead of taking a hand. So you don't arrive at what's happening; you keep the picture of what happened before. What's underneath is real — you see clearly, and what this is for when it works is plain: shining without needing credit.

Here's the way back. Give one custom or saying you already use somehow — something you say, something you make the same way each time — a lasting shape this week. Put it where it will be found again, or teach it once to somebody. The lasting form is the point, not the object: something you can point at instead of a memory. Hold it up and you'll see what you carry.

cells.tense: The threshold you already crossed is being described as one you stand before.
cells.act: open the door to the next thing on time, not early
cells.ask: Meet what's in this circle as itself — a word being used a new way, someone new standing in the old circle — and receive it as new before you file it. Note what changed, if it helps.
cells.core:
You read rooms well — the look before the sentence, the word older than the person saying it — and the room turns on that, and your account of yourself says that's just how it is. Fine. But what's actually happening is that each arrival is an arrival: not a continuation, not a rerun with new names on it.

When the next thing shows up where meaning is shared — a word used a new way, somebody new standing in the old circle — meet it as itself, not as this group's version of what happens. Nothing is being asked of the room. Notice what is newly here right now; that's the whole practice, and it's short. It's the difference between recognizing a moment and naming it before you look at it.

attempts.check: The record does not say this person has ever been read out of their own tradition, or what a custom costs them — the cores say only what a living eye does in a room that runs on shared meaning, never what happened to it there. A reader could reasonably say 'no, nothing here runs on inherited meaning and I'm not seeing anything first'; if that's true the asks still stand, because following a pattern to its edge and opening the next door are done with the person's own material, not the group's. The sentence serving me more than them is the note about other people hearing something they already know — it flatters the reader's position over the room's.
